Mr. Nam Giho, a new clerk, was the last to leave, and the copy was found in his coat. Haesu, a young clerk, saw the first clue. lines.master: A light burned at the list desk from eleven until one, and a sheet of thin paper proved the list had been copied. Mr. Nam Giho, a new clerk, was the last to leave, and the copy turned up sewn in his coat. Haesu, a young clerk, noticed the first clue. The Provisional Government was founded in Shanghai in April 1919, with Kim Gu as its police chief; his police guarded it and kept watch for spies. In 1940, Kim Gu became its chairman.

lines.junior: At dawn, Kim Gu's police stop Mr. Nam Giho down by the river.
lines.master: At dawn, Kim Gu's police catch up with Mr. Nam Giho by the river.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu comes back up the stairs.
lines.junior: Kim Gu climbs back up the stairs to the office.
lines.master: Kim Gu climbs the stairs back to the office.

lines.rookie: "Mr. Nam says he did nothing," he says. "Show me your proof."
lines.junior: "Mr. Nam says he did nothing," he says. "Show me your proof."
lines.master: "Mr. Nam insists he did nothing," he says. "Show me your proof."

lines.rookie: Mr. Nam says:
lines.junior: This is what Mr. Nam says:
lines.master: Mr. Nam's account:

lines.rookie:
Nobody was at the list desk last night.
Nothing was copied.
I went home at nine.
lines.junior:
"Nobody was at the list desk last night."
"Nothing was copied."
"I went home at nine."
lines.master:
"Not a soul was at the list desk last night."
"Nothing was copied."
"I went home at nine."

lines.rookie: Show Kim Gu that each thing Mr. Nam says is wrong.
lines.junior: Show Kim Gu why each thing Mr. Nam says is wrong.
lines.master: Prove to Kim Gu that each of Mr. Nam's claims is false.

lines.rookie: Each thing Mr. Nam says has one card that shows it is wrong.
lines.junior: For each thing Mr. Nam says, one card shows it is wrong.
lines.master: Each of Mr. Nam's claims is broken by exactly one card.

lines.rookie: Desk: Haesu's Note. Copy: the police report. Nine: the sign-out book.
lines.junior: The desk: Haesu's Note. The copy: the police report. Nine: the sign-out book.
lines.master: The desk: Haesu's Note. The copy: the police report. Nine o'clock: the sign-out book.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu nods. "Search his coat."
lines.junior: Kim Gu nods. "Search his coat."
lines.master: Kim Gu gives a nod. "Search his coat."

lines.rookie: Show one card for each thing Mr. Nam says.
lines.junior: Show one card for each thing that Mr. Nam says.
lines.master: Show one card against each of Mr. Nam's claims.

lines.rookie: Sewn inside Mr. Nam's coat is the copied list. It never left Shanghai.
lines.junior: The copied list is sewn inside Mr. Nam's coat, so it never left Shanghai.
lines.master: Sewn into the lining of Mr. Nam's coat is the copied list; it never left Shanghai.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu locks the real list and the copy in an iron box.
lines.junior: Kim Gu locks both the real list and the copy in an iron box.
lines.master: Kim Gu locks the real list and the copy away in an iron box.

lines.rookie: Show Kim Gu that Mr. Nam's words are wrong.
lines.junior: Show Kim Gu that what Mr. Nam says is wrong.
lines.master: Prove to Kim Gu that Mr. Nam's account is false.

lines.rookie: Without proof, I must let him go.
lines.junior: Without proof, I will have to let him go.
lines.master: Without proof, I have no choice but to let him go.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "He says nobody was at the list desk. Was someone?"
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "He says nobody was at the list desk. Was anyone there?"
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "He claims nobody was at the list desk. Was someone there?"

lines.rookie: Yes. The light went on at eleven. Half a new candle burned: until one.
lines.junior: Yes. The light went on at eleven, and half a new candle burned: until one.
lines.master: Yes. The light went on at eleven, and half a new candle burned away: until one.

lines.rookie: Two hours with our list.
lines.junior: Two whole hours with our list.
lines.master: Two long hours alone with our list.

lines.rookie: That does not show anyone at the desk.
lines.junior: That does not show anyone at the desk.
lines.master: That proves nobody was at the desk.

lines.rookie: Which card is about the candle and the light?
lines.junior: Which card tells about the candle and the light?
lines.master: Which card speaks of the candle and the light?

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "He says nothing was copied."
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "He says that nothing was copied."
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "He insists nothing was copied."

lines.rookie: This thin paper was under his copy. His pen pressed the names into it.
lines.junior: This thin paper lay under his copy, and his pen pressed the names into it.
lines.master: This thin paper lay beneath his copy; his pen pressed every name into it.

lines.rookie: So a copy was made. Where is it?
lines.junior: So a copy was made. But where is it?
lines.master: So a copy was made. Then where is it now?

lines.rookie: That does not show a copy.
lines.junior: That does not show a copy.
lines.master: That proves nothing about a copy.

lines.rookie: Which card is about the thin paper?
lines.junior: Which card tells about the thin paper?
lines.master: Which card speaks of the thin paper?

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "He says he went home at nine."
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "He says that he went home at nine."
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "He claims he went home at nine."

lines.rookie: The sign-out book says a quarter past one. Everyone else left before one.
lines.junior: The sign-out book says a quarter past one, and everyone else left before one.
lines.master: The sign-out book says a quarter past one; every other clerk had gone before one.

lines.rookie: And the guard has no key. It was Mr. Nam.
lines.junior: And the guard has no key, so it was Mr. Nam.
lines.master: And the guard holds no key. It was Mr. Nam.

lines.rookie: That does not show when he left.
lines.junior: That does not show when he left.
lines.master: That says nothing of when he left.

lines.rookie: Which card has the times the clerks left?
lines.junior: Which card shows the times the clerks left?
lines.master: Which card records when the clerks left?

lines.rookie: SEARCH HIS COAT
lines.junior: SEARCH HIS COAT
lines.master: SEARCH HIS COAT

lines.rookie: Mr. Nam Giho can never spy in this office again.
lines.junior: Mr. Nam Giho will never spy in this office again.
lines.master: Mr. Nam Giho will never again spy in this office.

lines.rookie: In 1940, Kim Gu became the chairman, the leader, of that government.
lines.junior: In 1940, Kim Gu became the chairman, the leader, of that government.
lines.master: In 1940, Kim Gu became chairman, the leader, of that same government.

lines.rookie: Nothing was copied.
lines.junior: Nothing was copied.
lines.master: Nothing was copied.

lines.rookie: I went home at nine.
lines.junior: I went home at nine.
lines.master: I went home at nine.
